box1Form.hoursHelperText: Used to calculate annual income from hourly rate
box1Form.holidayAllowanceTooltip: Enable if the entered salary includes 8% holiday allowance. Otherwise, the calculation uses only the entered salary, except when an applicable 30% ruling adds the allowance to total compensation. See the explanation below.
box1Form.olderAgeTooltip: Check if you are at or above state pension age (AOW). Different tax rates and no AOW premium apply.
box1Form.ruling30Tooltip: Tax-free allowance for skilled migrants. 30% of your salary becomes tax-free. Different income thresholds apply based on category.
box1Form.socialSecurityTooltip: Include Dutch social security contributions (AOW, ANW, WLZ). Most employees pay these unless exempt.
box1Form.resetMessage: This will clear all your entered data including income, hours, and tax settings. This action cannot be undone.

box1Result.taxableIncomeInfo: Income subject to taxation (after 30% ruling if applicable).
box1Result.payrollTaxInfo: Income tax withheld from your salary.
box1Result.socialSecurityInfo: Contributions for AOW, ANW, and WLZ.
box1Result.generalTaxCreditInfo: Algemene heffingskorting - basic tax credit for all taxpayers.

box3Result.estimatedTaxInfo: Projected Box 3 tax for the selected year using current assumptions.
box3Result.netAssetsInfo: Your savings and investments after subtracting deductible debts.
box3Result.taxableBaseInfo: Amount that remains after the tax-free allowance has been applied.
box3Result.totalAssetsInfo: Combined balances of your bank and investment accounts.
box3Result.debtsInfo: Deductible debts included in the Box 3 calculation.
box3Result.allowancesAppliedInfo: Standard tax-free allowance applied to your Box 3 assets.
box3Result.actualReturnDisclaimer: The tool does not calculate or compare actual returns. The Belastingdienst can use actual returns when that gives a lower result; the conditions and reporting process depend on the tax year.

box3Form.bankAccountsDesc: Add the balances of your Dutch checking and savings accounts on 1 January.
box3Form.investmentAccountsDesc: Include the market value of your investment or brokerage portfolios on 1 January.
box3Form.debtsDesc: List deductible debts, such as loans outstanding on 1 January.
box3Form.taxPartnerTooltip: If you have a fiscal partner, the tax-free threshold doubles.

modals.aboutText: incomeTaxNL estimates Dutch gross-to-net salary in Box 1 and tax on savings and investments in Box 3. Calculations run locally in your browser.
modals.howToUseTitle: How to use this Dutch income tax calculator
modals.howToUse1: Select Box 1 (salary calculator) or Box 3 (capital gains) using the toggle at the top.
modals.howToUse2: Enter your gross salary, savings, investments, and debts to calculate net income.
modals.howToUse3: Open the settings gear to tweak thresholds, return assumptions, or tax year.
modals.howToUse4: Review the results panel for your take home pay and detailed tax breakdown.
modals.originText: Navigating Dutch taxes used to be confusing for me. I built an elaborate spreadsheet to make sense of the rules, but it was too complex for friends and colleagues. This app is the friendlier version—same clarity, with explanations that anyone can follow.

guide.title: How this calculator estimates Dutch tax
guide.years: Tax years: Box 1 2019–2026; Box 3 2023–2026. Select the year in the calculator. The current-year sources below cover 2026; earlier years use their own calculation settings.
guide.salaryTitle: From gross salary to net pay
guide.salaryText: Box 1 converts your gross salary to an annual amount, applies the selected year’s income tax brackets and, when enabled, national insurance contributions, then applies general and employment tax credits. Hourly input also uses your hours per week. The result is an estimate for salary income, not a full income tax return.
guide.salarySource: Belastingdienst: Box 1 income tax and rates (Dutch)
guide.holidayText: Check whether your input already includes holiday allowance. The calculator uses an 8% allowance assumption and separates it when included. Without the 30% ruling, leaving this option off calculates only the salary entered; it does not add a separate holiday payment. With an applicable ruling, the calculation includes an 8% allowance in total compensation. The allowance and net-pay figures are estimates, not a payslip calculation of the actual payout.
guide.rulingText: Enable the ruling only to model an applicable expat arrangement. Choose the general, under-30 master’s graduate or scientific researcher category to use the corresponding salary threshold. The calculation limits the exempt amount using the selected year’s settings. These inputs do not check all eligibility conditions, an approval’s duration or transitional rules; confirm your situation with your employer and the Belastingdienst.
guide.rulingSource: Belastingdienst: eligibility for the expat scheme
guide.box3Text: Enter bank balances, investments and eligible debts as at 1 January of the selected tax year. This calculator estimates tax using deemed returns by asset category, a debt threshold, the tax-free allowance and the tax-partner setting. The taxable share of the calculated return is multiplied by the Box 3 tax rate. Custom rate settings change the estimate. For 2026, bank and debt return percentages are provisional.
guide.actualText: The tool does not calculate or compare actual returns. The Belastingdienst can use actual returns when that gives a lower result; the conditions and reporting process depend on the tax year.
guide.actualSource: Belastingdienst: actual returns and how to report them (Dutch)
guide.limitsText: This tool calculates gross-to-net pay, not net-to-gross. It has no inputs for pension deductions, mortgage deductions, other income or a complete tax return. The age and national insurance switches are simplified, and the year you reach state pension age can require a different calculation. Box 1 and Box 3 are separate estimates; Box 3 income is not used to recalculate Box 1 tax credits. Check the result against your payslip and the official rules for your tax year.
